goal: DEPTH: sub-sections / config sections in real integration with the backend — raise real coverage and capability levels
must_build: Every page in ui-spec/azure/subscriptions.json (29 pages; nav: Overview, Activity log, Access control (IAM), Tags, Diagnose and solve problems, Security, Events, Cost Management, Billing, Settings, Help)
Backend: ARM subscription (DEFAULT_SUBSCRIPTION in azure/kit/arm.js): overview, resource providers, IAM role assignments (test_azure_rbac_core.py)
List / create / detail / edit / delete round-trips through the native API the SDK and CLI use
always: Every page wired to the native API on /_wire (no static data); liveness fixtures for every list/detail page
core/capabilities/azure/subscriptions.json: one entry per console section with an honest level + tests; tests/conformance/test_capabilities.py must pass
Capability feature ids MUST start with 'azure.' (e.g. 'azure.subscriptions.<section>') — ids share one namespace with the AWS registry
Read the 'Cloud lenses' section of consoles/AGENT-UI.md first — use this cloud's kit, not Cloudscape

depth_targets.title: Subscription overview (get, rename) over ARM
limitations: Vyomi simulates exactly one subscription — renaming it changes the one simulated subscription's display name rather than creating or listing an independent additional subscription. Offer, Offer ID, Parent management group and Secure score are not modeled.

depth_targets.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity.

depth_targets.title: Access control (IAM) — role assignments and definitions
limitations: Role assignments/definitions are the generic ARM catalog store (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions) and no access decisions are evaluated — every data-plane call succeeds regardless of what is assigned. Deny assignments and classic administrators are always empty.

depth_targets.title: Deployments (Microsoft.Resources/deployments) history, subscription scope
limitations: Deployment creation stores whatever template/parameters/mode the client sends and returns Succeeded immediately — there is no template-language evaluation (no parameter/variable resolution, no dependsOn ordering) and nothing is actually provisioned from it; the underlying resources still need their own PUT calls. Cancel and Redeploy are not simulated.

depth_targets.title: Usage + quotas
limitations: Per-resource-type, per-location compute/network quota (Microsoft.Compute usages) is not modeled — Vyomi has no fixed quantity caps to report against.

depth_targets.title: Diagnose and solve problems, Security, Events, Advisor recommendations, Invoices, Partner information, Programmatic deployment, Billing properties, Preview features, Policies, Management certificates, My permissions, Deployment stacks, Support + Troubleshooting
limitations: These subscription blade menu items are billing-account, Microsoft Defender, Azure Policy, Microsoft Entra or classic Service Management features with no Vyomi backend.

note:
DEPTH PASS (the base console is merged). Goal: turn this service's sub-sections and config sections into REAL backend integrations. For EACH capability entry listed in `depth_targets` decide:
  BUILD — Vyomi can model it in the shared core (state + native API semantics): implement it in core/<svc>_core.py (and the offline route if offline lacks it), add conformance checks in tests/conformance/, raise the entry's level in core/capabilities/<cloud>/<svc>.json (not_simulated→limited/full, config_only→limited/full where now ENFORCED, limited→full where a limitation is removed), wire the console section to it with a UI↔native-API round trip in consoles/tests/smoke-<cloud>.mjs and a "live" fixture for any list/detail page.
  KEEP HONEST — only if it needs something a local simulator cannot run (a separate product, real hardware/network, billing, third-party identity): leave it NotSimulated and put the concrete reason in the entry's `limitations`.
Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. Real coverage must go UP; nothing may regress: fidelity ≥ 90%, every capability claim true on nano AND offline, smokes green. Do not edit consoles/honest-allowlist.json or .github/.
House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.
